stories.headline: Files Relating to India's Largest Nuclear Plant Kudankulam Exposed in Data Breach
stories.what: Sensitive files relating to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant — India's largest nuclear facility — have been exposed in a data breach, Reuters has exclusively reported. The breach raises serious questions about cybersecurity protocols at one of India's most critical pieces of national infrastructure. Kudankulam, located in Tamil Nadu and built with Russian cooperation, generates a significant share of India's nuclear power capacity.
stories.lens: A data breach at India's largest nuclear power plant is a direct national security concern — any exposure of facility files could compromise plant safety, operational security, and India's broader nuclear programme.
stories.article:
Sensitive files relating to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, India's largest nuclear facility, have been exposed in a data breach, according to an exclusive Reuters report. The revelation raises urgent questions about the cybersecurity posture of one of India's most strategically critical infrastructure assets.

Kudankulam, situated on the southern tip of Tamil Nadu and constructed with Russian technical and financial cooperation, is a cornerstone of India's civil nuclear power programme. The plant operates multiple reactors and contributes significantly to India's nuclear energy generation capacity. Any compromise of its operational or technical files carries serious implications for both plant safety and national security.

This is not the first time Kudankulam has faced a cybersecurity scare — the facility was previously linked to a malware incident that drew significant attention. The latest data breach, as reported by Reuters, suggests that the vulnerabilities at the plant may be deeper or more persistent than previously acknowledged. The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, which operates the plant, has not immediately responded publicly to the latest report.

The incident is likely to intensify scrutiny of cybersecurity standards across India's nuclear sector and could prompt calls from Parliament and security experts for a comprehensive audit of digital defences at sensitive installations. For a country expanding its nuclear energy ambitions, protecting the digital integrity of its plants is as critical as their physical security.
key_facts: Files from Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant exposed in data breach
Reuters reported the breach exclusively
Kudankulam is India's largest nuclear power plant, located in Tamil Nadu
Plant was built with Russian cooperation

stories.headline: ICC Revamps Cricket World Cup Format — India vs Pakistan Double Header on the Cards
stories.what: The ICC is planning a significant shake-up to the Cricket World Cup format, with reports suggesting the revamp could create the possibility of an India vs Pakistan double header — two matches between the sides in the same tournament. The Guardian reported the development, which follows the ICC's already-announced changes to the World Cup structure. For cricket's commercial ecosystem, an additional India-Pakistan fixture would be among the most valuable sporting events on the planet.
stories.lens: An India vs Pakistan double header at a Cricket World Cup would be the biggest spectacle in world cricket — and for Indian fans, it would mean two chances to witness the sport's greatest rivalry on the grandest stage.
stories.article:
The International Cricket Council is planning a fresh shake-up to the Cricket World Cup format that could put an India vs Pakistan double header firmly on the cards, according to a report by The Guardian. The proposed changes would restructure the tournament in a way that makes it possible for the two arch-rivals to meet twice in the same edition of the competition.

India and Pakistan matches are consistently the most-watched cricket events in the world, generating extraordinary television audiences, ticket demand, and commercial revenue. The prospect of two such fixtures in a single World Cup would be a landmark moment for the sport, and the ICC's willingness to structure the tournament in a way that enables this outcome reflects the commercial logic driving much of modern cricket administration.

The revamp appears to be part of a broader rethinking of how the World Cup is organised, following previous changes to the number of teams and the group stage format. The specific structural details of the new format were not fully outlined in the available reporting, but the India-Pakistan double header possibility is the headline element that has captured immediate attention.

For Indian fans, the news is tantalising. India-Pakistan World Cup encounters have produced some of cricket's most memorable moments, and the possibility of two such meetings in a single tournament would dominate the build-up to the next edition. The ICC is expected to formally announce the format changes in due course.
key_facts: ICC planning a Cricket World Cup format revamp
India vs Pakistan double header possible under new format
The Guardian reported the development

stories.headline: Trump Wanted a '20% Hormuz Toll' — How Gulf Leaders Shut It Down in 24 Hours
stories.what: US President Donald Trump reportedly sought to impose a 20% toll on shipping passing through the Strait of Hormuz, a proposal that would have dramatically raised costs for global trade — including India's oil imports. Gulf leaders moved swiftly to shut down the idea within 24 hours, according to reports, resisting a plan that would have effectively taxed much of the world's energy trade. The episode illustrates the intense diplomatic maneuvering around the strait as US military strikes on Iran continue.
stories.lens: The Strait of Hormuz is the artery through which a large portion of India's oil imports flow — any toll or blockade there translates almost directly into higher fuel prices at Indian pumps.
stories.article:
Donald Trump's administration floated the idea of levying a 20% toll on all shipping passing through the Strait of Hormuz — a proposal that, if enacted, would have represented one of the most sweeping interventions in global maritime trade in modern history. The plan was reportedly shut down by Gulf leaders within 24 hours, underlining both the audacity of the proposal and the limits of US leverage over its Gulf partners.

The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil chokepoint, with a vast share of global crude exports — including a significant portion of India's imports — transiting through its narrow waters. A 20% toll would have added enormous costs to every barrel of oil, every LNG shipment, and a wide range of other commodities passing through the strait, with knock-on effects for consumer prices worldwide.

Gulf states, whose economies are fundamentally tied to unimpeded access through Hormuz, pushed back hard against the proposal. Their rapid rejection of the toll idea demonstrated that even close US allies in the region have firm red lines when it comes to their core economic interests and regional sovereignty.

The episode played out against the backdrop of continuing US strikes on Iran and Iranian threats to block trade routes — a volatile combination that has kept oil markets on edge. For India, which imports a large share of its energy from Gulf producers, the stability of the strait remains a matter of direct national economic interest, and New Delhi will have been relieved to see the toll proposal collapse so swiftly.
key_facts: Trump reportedly proposed a 20% toll on Strait of Hormuz shipping
Gulf leaders rejected the proposal within 24 hours
Iran has threatened to block additional trade routes
Oil, LNG, fertilisers and other key commodities pass through Hormuz

stories.headline: 'I Intend to Kill Muslims': Indian Mall Worker Stabbed 15 Times in US
stories.what: An Indian man working at a mall in Utah, USA, was stabbed 15 times by a man who reportedly declared 'I intend to kill Muslims' and asked the victim 'Are you Muslim?' before the attack. The victim survived the hate crime attack, which has drawn widespread attention in India and among Indian-American communities. The incident is among the most serious anti-Muslim hate crimes targeting an Indian national in the United States in recent memory.
stories.lens: The targeted stabbing of an Indian worker in the US on religious grounds is a stark reminder of the hate crime risks faced by the Indian diaspora abroad, and will heighten anxiety among Indian families with relatives in America.
stories.article:
An Indian man working at a shopping mall in Utah was stabbed 15 times in what authorities are treating as a religiously motivated hate crime, after his attacker allegedly asked 'Are you Muslim?' before declaring 'I intend to kill Muslims' and launching the assault. The victim survived the brutal attack, which has sparked outrage in India and among Indian communities in the United States.

The incident unfolded at a US mall when the assailant, described as a Utah man, confronted the Indian worker with a direct religious challenge before carrying out the stabbing. The victim's survival after 15 stab wounds is being described as fortunate, and he is reported to be receiving medical treatment. Authorities have taken the suspect into custody.

The attack has prompted a sharp response in India, with the Times of India, NDTV and India Today all carrying prominent coverage of the incident. It raises uncomfortable questions about the safety of Indian workers and members of the Indian diaspora in the United States, particularly those who are Muslim or perceived to be Muslim in an environment of rising anti-Muslim sentiment in parts of the country.

The Indian government has not yet made a formal statement on the incident, but incidents of this nature typically draw consular attention and diplomatic representations. For the millions of Indians living and working in the United States, the attack is a sobering reminder of the vulnerabilities they can face, and will add to growing concerns about the safety environment for minority communities in America.
key_facts: Indian mall worker stabbed 15 times in Utah, USA
Attacker said 'I intend to kill Muslims' before the assault
Attacker asked 'Are you Muslim?' before attacking
Victim survived the attack

stories.headline: India U19 Opening Pair Puts on 295-Run Stand Against Sri Lanka, Nears World Record
stories.what: India's Under-19 opening pair came agonisingly close to breaking the world record for an opening partnership in youth cricket, putting on a 295-run stand against Sri Lanka. The mammoth partnership is one of the highest ever recorded in U19 cricket and set up what is expected to be a dominant total for India. The performance signals the depth of young batting talent coming through India's cricketing pipeline.
stories.lens: A near-world-record opening stand by India's U19 pair is a thrilling glimpse of the next generation of Indian cricket talent — the players who will be competing for senior caps in the years ahead.
stories.article:
India's Under-19 opening pair produced a stunning 295-run partnership against Sri Lanka, falling just short of the world record for an opening stand in youth international cricket. The knock, reported by Wisden, underlines the extraordinary depth of batting talent emerging from India's junior cricket system.

The 295-run stand is one of the largest opening partnerships in U19 cricket history, and its proximity to the world record made it a landmark performance that will be talked about for years. The partnership overwhelmed Sri Lanka's bowling attack and set the platform for what was expected to be a very large team total, putting India in complete command of the match.

India's U19 programme has long been one of the most productive pathways to senior international cricket, producing a string of players who have gone on to represent the national side. A record-threatening opening stand of this magnitude will inevitably draw attention from national selectors and cricket analysts watching the next wave of talent develop.

For Indian cricket fans, the performance is cause for genuine excitement — a reminder that even as the senior team navigates its own pressures, the conveyor belt of talent from India's youth system continues to deliver. The names of the two openers will be ones to watch as they progress through the domestic and A-team cricket structure in the coming seasons.
key_facts: India U19 opening pair put on 295-run stand vs Sri Lanka
Partnership came close to breaking the world record for U19 cricket
Match was against Sri Lanka in U19 cricket

stories.headline: Trade Setup for July 16: Nifty Battles 24,200 Resistance in Range-Bound Market
stories.what: Markets head into July 16 with the Nifty navigating a range-bound phase, facing key resistance at 24,200 and a crucial pivot level at 24,250, according to Moneycontrol and NDTV Profit. The index has a further resistance zone at 24,400. Traders and investors will be watching these technical levels closely at the opening bell, with the market's ability to sustain above resistance likely to determine short-term direction. Global cues and domestic macro data will also factor into early trade.
stories.lens: For retail investors and traders, knowing where the Nifty's key resistance and support levels sit helps calibrate buy or sell decisions for the trading session ahead.
stories.article:
The Indian equity market heads into the July 16 session with the Nifty facing a critical test at key resistance levels, according to pre-market analysis from Moneycontrol and NDTV Profit. The index has been navigating a range-bound phase, and the coming session will see it battle resistance at 24,200, with the pivot level pegged at 24,250 and a more significant barrier at 24,400.

Market watchers have identified these levels as the lines in the sand for bulls and bears alike. A sustained move above 24,400 could open up fresh upside momentum, while failure to breach 24,200 may invite renewed selling pressure. The broader market tone will be shaped by global overnight cues, currency movements, and any fresh domestic macro data.

The session comes after a week that has seen significant macro developments — including India's current account deficit data for May and the implementation of the India-UK trade deal — all of which feed into the investment climate. Foreign institutional investor activity will be closely monitored, as will movements in the banking and IT sectors, which carry the heaviest weight in index composition.

Retail participation in Indian equity markets has grown sharply in recent years, making pre-market trade setups increasingly relevant to a wide audience. Analysts recommend that traders watch the 24,200-24,400 range as the key battleground for the session, with any decisive breakout or breakdown likely to set the tone for the rest of the week.
key_facts: Nifty faces resistance at 24,200 heading into July 16 session
Pivot level at 24,250; key resistance at 24,400
Market described as range-bound
Global cues and FII activity will be closely watched

stories.headline: India's Current Account Slips to $2 Billion Deficit in May as Trade Gap Widens
stories.what: India recorded a current account deficit of $2 billion in May as the gap between imports and exports widened, according to data reported by The Economic Times. The current account is a broad measure of a country's trade in goods, services, and transfers with the rest of the world. A widening trade gap, driven by higher import bills relative to export earnings, pushed the balance into deficit territory for the month. The development will be closely watched by policymakers at the Reserve Bank of India.
stories.lens: A rising current account deficit can put pressure on the rupee and India's foreign exchange reserves, affecting everything from import costs to inflation for ordinary consumers.
stories.article:
India's current account slipped into a deficit of $2 billion in May, as a widening trade gap weighed on the country's external balance, data reported by The Economic Times showed. The current account — which captures trade in goods and services, income flows, and transfers — moved into the red as import growth outpaced export earnings during the month.

The trade gap, which forms the largest component of the current account, has been under pressure from elevated global commodity prices and robust domestic demand for imports. While India's services exports, particularly from the IT sector, continue to provide a partial cushion, they were insufficient to fully offset the merchandise trade shortfall in May.

A current account deficit of this scale, while not alarming in isolation, is a metric closely tracked by the Reserve Bank of India and financial markets. A sustained or widening deficit typically exerts downward pressure on the rupee and can draw down foreign exchange reserves if not offset by capital inflows.

The data comes against a backdrop of India's trade performance coming under scrutiny. A separate editorial in The Hindu noted export gains in India's June trade data, suggesting some improvement in momentum heading into the summer months. Policymakers will be watching whether the May deficit proves to be a temporary blip or the start of a renewed widening trend.

For India's macroeconomic managers, keeping the current account deficit within a comfortable range remains a key priority, particularly as global uncertainties around energy prices and supply chains persist.
key_facts: India's current account deficit stood at $2 billion in May
Deficit driven by a widening trade gap
Services exports provide partial cushion but insufficient to offset shortfall
RBI and markets will monitor trend closely

stories.headline: JPMorgan Edges Closer to Historic $1 Trillion Market Value Milestone
stories.what: JPMorgan Chase is moving closer to becoming the first bank in history to reach a market capitalisation of $1 trillion, according to a report by The Economic Times. No bank anywhere in the world has previously crossed this threshold, making it a landmark in global financial history if achieved. The development reflects the outsized growth of US banking giants and has implications for global capital markets, including how institutional investors allocate funds across sectors and geographies.
stories.lens: As one of the largest foreign institutional investors active in Indian markets, JPMorgan's valuation trajectory and global standing directly influences capital flows into India.
stories.article:
JPMorgan Chase is inching toward a milestone that no bank in history has ever achieved — a market capitalisation of $1 trillion. The American banking behemoth's surging valuation has put it on a trajectory that, if sustained, would place it in an exclusive club currently occupied only by the world's largest technology companies.

No bank globally has previously reached this threshold. JPMorgan's march toward a $1 trillion market cap reflects a combination of strong earnings, dominant market share across investment banking, consumer banking, and asset management, and investor confidence in its long-term strategic positioning under CEO Jamie Dimon.

The milestone carries broader significance for global capital markets. As one of the most systemically important financial institutions in the world, JPMorgan's health and valuation are closely watched by regulators, investors, and central banks. A bank of this scale reaching the $1 trillion mark would underscore the growing concentration of financial power in a handful of US institutions.

For India, the development is relevant given JPMorgan's prominent role as a foreign institutional investor and its inclusion of Indian government bonds in its global bond indices — a decision that unlocked substantial foreign inflows into Indian debt markets. The bank's expanding footprint in India, across investment banking and markets advisory, means its financial strength and risk appetite have a tangible bearing on domestic capital markets.
key_facts: JPMorgan approaching $1 trillion market capitalisation
No bank in history has previously reached this milestone
JPMorgan included Indian government bonds in its global bond indices
Development signals growing dominance of major US financial institutions

stories.headline: India-UK Trade Deal Takes Effect: What Gets Cheaper and Which Sectors Gain
stories.what: The India-UK free trade agreement has officially kicked in, marking one of India's most significant bilateral trade pacts in recent years. The deal cuts tariffs on a wide range of goods and opens up services trade between the two economies. UK-made goods including Scotch whisky and cars are expected to become cheaper in India, while Indian textiles, pharmaceuticals, and IT services stand to gain greater access to the British market. The pact also comes with UK backing for India's security concerns, described as a deal built on trust.
stories.lens: From cheaper imported goods to new export opportunities for Indian manufacturers and IT professionals, this trade deal has direct and wide-ranging consequences for Indian businesses and consumers alike.
stories.article:
The India-UK Free Trade Agreement came into force, ushering in a new era of bilateral commerce that slashes tariffs on hundreds of product categories and expands market access for services on both sides. It is one of the most consequential trade deals India has signed in decades, covering a relationship worth tens of billions of dollars annually.

For Indian consumers, the deal promises lower prices on imported British goods, with sectors like Scotch whisky, automobiles, and high-end consumer products among those expected to see tariff reductions. On the flip side, Indian exporters in textiles, leather, gems and jewellery, pharmaceuticals, and engineering goods are positioned to gain meaningfully from reduced barriers into the UK market.

The services dimension is equally significant. India's booming IT sector and its large diaspora of professionals stand to benefit from more favourable terms for mobility and market access. The UK's financial, legal, and educational services, meanwhile, are expected to find greater entry points into India's growing economy.

In a notable diplomatic dimension, the UK has publicly backed India's security concerns, with officials describing the agreement as one grounded in mutual trust rather than purely transactional interests. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who also hailed a separate India-EU trade framework in the same period, called trade deals of this nature "fair, equitable, and balanced."

Trade analysts see the India-UK deal as a template for India's broader push to diversify its trade relationships amid shifting global supply chains, with the agreement sending a strong signal to other potential partners about New Delhi's readiness to engage on ambitious terms.
key_facts: India-UK FTA officially comes into force
Tariffs cut on goods including Scotch whisky and cars entering India
Indian textiles, pharma, and IT services gain UK market access
UK backs India's security concerns; deal described as trust-based

stories.headline: India Emerges as Strategic AI Transformation Market for Global IT Firms
stories.what: India is increasingly being seen as a strategic market for artificial intelligence transformation by global IT companies, even as they pursue international business opportunities, according to The New Indian Express. The country's large talent pool, growing digital infrastructure, and expanding enterprise adoption of AI are driving this shift in positioning. IT majors are no longer treating India purely as a delivery hub but as a significant market in its own right for AI-led services and solutions.
stories.lens: For India's IT sector and its millions of tech workers, this shift means more high-value AI jobs and projects could be anchored domestically rather than exclusively serving foreign clients.
stories.article:
India has emerged as a strategic market for artificial intelligence transformation among global IT firms, marking a significant shift in how the country is perceived within the technology industry. Rather than being viewed solely as an offshore delivery destination, India is now being targeted as a major consumer and adopter of AI-driven enterprise solutions.

The change is being driven by several converging factors: a vast and technically skilled workforce capable of building and deploying AI systems, rapid growth in digital infrastructure, and increasing appetite among Indian enterprises across banking, healthcare, retail, and manufacturing to integrate AI into their operations. Global IT firms are responding by deepening their India-facing business units and product offerings.

This repositioning carries significant implications for the broader Indian economy. As AI transformation becomes central to enterprise strategy globally, having India as both a delivery hub and a primary market means that domestic IT companies and their employees are better positioned to capture value closer to home. It could also accelerate the development of India-specific AI applications tailored to local languages, regulatory environments, and business needs.

The trend aligns with India's stated ambitions to become a global AI powerhouse. Government initiatives around data governance, compute infrastructure, and AI skill development are creating an enabling environment. Industry observers note that the next wave of IT-sector growth in India may be driven as much by domestic AI adoption as by exports.
key_facts: India positioned as strategic AI transformation market, not just delivery hub
Driven by large tech talent pool, digital infrastructure growth, and enterprise AI adoption
Global IT firms deepening India-facing AI business units
Aligns with India's national ambitions to lead in artificial intelligence

stories.headline: Indian AI startup Emergent joins unicorn club after raising $130 million at $1.5 billion valuation
stories.what: Emergent, an Indian artificial intelligence startup, has become a unicorn after closing a $130 million funding round that values the company at $1.5 billion. The milestone adds a new name to India's unicorn list at a time when investor sentiment around applied AI startups has been surging globally. Emergent's raise underscores growing international investor confidence in Indian AI ventures capable of achieving billion-dollar scale.
stories.lens: Every new Indian AI unicorn strengthens the country's case as a global AI product hub — not just a services outsourcing destination.
stories.article:
Emergent, an Indian AI startup, has officially entered the unicorn club after raising $130 million in a fresh funding round that pegged its valuation at $1.5 billion, NDTV Profit and Moneycontrol reported. The milestone makes Emergent one of the few Indian AI-native companies to cross the billion-dollar valuation threshold.

The raise arrives as global venture capital flows into applied artificial intelligence companies continue at an elevated pace. Investors have been seeking out startups with demonstrable AI products and enterprise traction, and Emergent's ability to command a $1.5 billion valuation signals it has cleared that bar with its backers.

India's unicorn pipeline had slowed considerably after the funding winter of 2022-23, making Emergent's emergence particularly notable. A fresh AI-focused unicorn suggests the domestic startup ecosystem is finding new momentum, this time driven by artificial intelligence rather than the consumer internet plays that defined the last generation of Indian billion-dollar companies.

The development also reinforces India's growing reputation as a serious incubator of AI talent and product companies. With the government simultaneously making major bets on semiconductor infrastructure, the Emergent milestone fits into a broader narrative of India positioning itself as a full-stack technology nation — from chips to AI applications.
key_facts: Emergent raised $130 million in its latest round
Valuation set at $1.5 billion — unicorn status achieved
Emergent is an Indian AI-native startup
One of few Indian AI product companies to reach unicorn scale

stories.headline: India and EU back diverse supply chains and deep-tech startup ties after technology talks
stories.what: India and the European Union have jointly endorsed diversified supply chains and pledged deeper cooperation on technology and trade following their Trade and Technology Council talks. Both sides signalled momentum on a long-pending Free Trade Agreement and flagged new avenues for deep-tech startup partnerships. The meeting reflects the shared strategic interest of both blocs in reducing dependence on single-country supply chains, particularly for critical technologies.
stories.lens: An India-EU deep-tech startup corridor could open European markets and funding to Indian technology companies while giving India access to EU research and manufacturing ecosystems.
stories.article:
India and the European Union have affirmed their commitment to building resilient, diversified supply chains after a round of Trade and Technology Council talks, India Today reported. The joint statement backing supply chain diversification comes as both sides seek to reduce strategic exposure to concentrated manufacturing hubs.

Beyond trade, the talks produced significant momentum on the long-stalled India-EU Free Trade Agreement, with officials describing the TTC meeting as a booster for FTA negotiations. A deep-tech startup partnership between Indian and European companies also emerged as a priority area, potentially creating new channels for funding, market access, and research collaboration.

The broader geopolitical context is hard to miss. Both India and the EU have been actively working to reduce dependence on Chinese manufacturing for semiconductors, critical minerals, and telecommunications equipment. A formal India-EU supply chain and deep-tech framework would add institutional weight to those individual efforts.

For India's technology sector, the prospect of a structured deep-tech startup partnership with Europe is particularly consequential. It could accelerate Indian startups' access to European customers and regulatory frameworks, while giving EU firms a route into India's fast-growing digital economy. The next steps in formalising these commitments will be closely watched.
key_facts: India and EU back supply chain diversification at TTC meeting
FTA negotiations given fresh momentum by the talks
Deep-tech startup partnership flagged as a priority area
Meeting held under the India-EU Trade and Technology Council framework

stories.headline: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw: India struggles to create globally disruptive innovation
stories.what: Biocon founder and prominent industrialist Kiran Mazumdar Shaw has argued that India faces a structural challenge in producing the kind of globally disruptive innovation that reshapes industries. Her comments, reported by CNBC TV18, touch on a debate that is increasingly central to India's technology policy — whether the country is building genuinely world-changing companies or primarily optimising existing models for the domestic market.
stories.lens: When one of India's most successful entrepreneurs says the country isn't producing global disruptors, it is a candid challenge to policymakers and startup founders to think beyond incremental wins.
stories.article:
Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, the founder of Biocon and one of India's most prominent business voices, has said the country struggles to create globally disruptive innovation — a pointed observation from someone who has built one of India's rare globally competitive companies from scratch. Her comments were reported by CNBC TV18.

The critique is not new, but carries weight coming from Shaw. India has produced a large number of unicorn startups over the past decade, yet most have been built around adapting existing global business models — food delivery, e-commerce, fintech — for the Indian market. Genuinely category-defining innovations that reshape global industries have been rare.

Shaw's argument touches on structural factors that analysts have long identified: risk aversion in research and development investment, a talent pipeline that is large but often channelled toward services rather than deep research, and an innovation ecosystem that has historically rewarded growth and scale over fundamental breakthroughs.

The conversation is particularly timely as India pours billions into semiconductor manufacturing and AI infrastructure. The question Shaw implicitly raises is whether new capital alone will produce disruptive innovation, or whether deeper changes to research culture, university-industry linkages, and patient capital are required. Her voice adds urgency to a debate that India's technology sector cannot afford to treat as purely rhetorical.
key_facts: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw says India struggles to create globally disruptive innovation
Shaw is the founder of Biocon, one of India's rare global-scale innovators
Comments reported by CNBC TV18
Critique centres on India's innovation ecosystem and R&D culture

stories.headline: Women founders say AI, conviction and fearlessness will power India's next startup wave
stories.what: Indian women startup founders have said that artificial intelligence, strong conviction, and a fearless approach to risk-taking will define the country's next generation of successful ventures, according to a CNBC TV18 report. The perspectives were shared under the 'Future Female Forward' platform, highlighting the growing voice and ambition of women entrepreneurs in India's technology and startup ecosystem.
stories.lens: Women founders shaping the narrative around India's next startup wave signals a maturation of the ecosystem — and sets expectations for who gets funded and whose ideas get built.
stories.article:
Indian women founders have declared that artificial intelligence, personal conviction, and a willingness to embrace risk without fear will be the defining traits of India's next wave of successful startups, CNBC TV18 reported as part of its Future Female Forward series. The comments reflect the views of women entrepreneurs who are increasingly visible and influential in a startup ecosystem that has historically been male-dominated.

The emphasis on AI is unsurprising given the current investment climate, but the founders' framing goes beyond technology — they are arguing for a cultural shift in how Indian entrepreneurs approach uncertainty and scale. Conviction and fearlessness, as they describe it, are about backing ideas that lack obvious precedent in the Indian market rather than iterating on proven global playbooks.

The observations come at a moment when India's startup ecosystem is actively recalibrating after a difficult funding period. The women founders' message is in part a call for investors and institutions to expand the tent — to fund more diverse ideas, from more diverse founders, pursuing more ambitious goals.

For India's broader technology narrative, the Future Female Forward platform surfaces a dimension that often goes underreported: the growing cohort of women building serious technology companies. Their collective view that AI will be the central tool of the next startup wave aligns with the direction of capital and policy — but their insistence on conviction and fearlessness is a reminder that the human element remains decisive.
key_facts: Women founders identify AI as the key driver of India's next startup wave
Conviction and fearlessness cited as essential entrepreneurial traits
Comments gathered under CNBC TV18's Future Female Forward platform

stories.headline: India bets ₹1.27 lakh crore on Semicon Mission 2.0 to break China's grip on chip manufacturing
stories.what: The Union Cabinet has approved ₹1.27 lakh crore for India's Semicon Mission 2.0, a massive push to build domestic semiconductor manufacturing and chip design capabilities. The move is aimed squarely at reducing India's dependence on Chinese supply chains for smartphone and electronics components. It represents one of the largest single technology-sector commitments in Indian government history, and positions India as a serious contender in the global chip race.
stories.lens: Semiconductors are inside every smartphone, car, and appliance Indians use — this ₹1.27 lakh crore bet determines whether those chips are ever made in India.
stories.article:
India's Union Cabinet has cleared ₹1.27 lakh crore for Semicon Mission 2.0, the government's most ambitious attempt yet to establish a self-sufficient semiconductor ecosystem and wrest electronics supply-chain leverage away from China. The approval covers investments in chip fabrication, advanced packaging, and enhanced domestic chip design infrastructure.

The scale of the commitment signals a fundamental shift in India's industrial strategy. For years, India has remained almost entirely dependent on imported semiconductors — most routed through Chinese manufacturing networks — to feed its booming smartphone and consumer electronics market. The new mission directly targets that vulnerability, with an emphasis on both attracting global foundries and nurturing homegrown design talent.

The move also builds on the earlier Semicon India programme and comes as global chipmakers accelerate efforts to diversify away from Taiwan and China. India is competing with incentive packages being offered by the United States, Japan, and the European Union to land major semiconductor facilities.

For the Indian technology ecosystem, the implications are profound. A domestic chip design and manufacturing base could eventually lower costs for device makers, create high-skill engineering jobs, and give India strategic leverage in an industry increasingly at the centre of geopolitical competition. Whether the capital translates into operational fabs within this decade will be the critical test of the mission's success.
key_facts: Cabinet approved ₹1.27 lakh crore for Semicon Mission 2.0
Mission targets chip design and semiconductor manufacturing buildout
Aimed at reducing India's reliance on Chinese electronics supply chains
Equivalent to approximately $13.3 billion

stories.headline: Bihar Woman and Boyfriend Hire Contract Killer to Murder Husband on Train
stories.what: A shocking murder case has emerged from Bihar, where a woman and her boyfriend allegedly hired a contract killer to murder her husband aboard a train. The killing on a moving train points to a premeditated and cold-blooded conspiracy. Police have been investigating the case and arrests have been made in connection with the crime. The incident has drawn attention to the alarming phenomenon of contract killings and crimes of passion in the state.
stories.lens: A contract killing executed on a moving train — one of India's most public spaces — exposes both the brazenness of organised crime networks and the vulnerability of passengers to premeditated violence.
stories.article:
A Bihar woman and her boyfriend allegedly hired a contract killer to murder her husband on a train, in a case that has stunned investigators with its cold premeditation and brazen execution. Police have confirmed the arrests in connection with the killing, which was carried out aboard a moving train.

The conspiracy, as investigators have pieced it together, involved the woman and her boyfriend contracting a hitman to carry out the murder, apparently to facilitate their relationship. The choice of a train as the location for the crime — a busy, public space — reflects either a calculated attempt to obscure responsibility or a disturbing disregard for the risks of discovery.

Contract killings, often rooted in property disputes, personal rivalries, or illicit relationships, have been a recurring problem in Bihar and neighbouring states. This case, however, stands out for its audacity — the use of a hired killer on public transport and the apparent involvement of a spouse plotting against her own husband.

Police are continuing their investigation to determine the full chain of conspiracy, identify all those involved, and understand how the killing was coordinated. The case has once again raised concerns about crime and safety on India's vast railway network, which carries millions of passengers every day.

Murder carried out on a moving train
Arrests have been made in the case

Jharkhand has seen persistent concerns about law and order, and crimes against women remain a deeply troubling pattern nationally. Advocates for women's safety have long argued that faster arrests and stringent prosecution are essential to deterring such crimes.

Ranchi police are expected to file a chargesheet in the case as investigations progress. The arrests are being closely watched by women's rights groups and civil society organisations who have demanded swift judicial action and robust support for the survivor.

stories.headline: Sonam Wangchuk Hunger Strike: Delhi HC Plea Warns He May Die in 2 Days
stories.what: Climate activist and innovator Sonam Wangchuk's ongoing hunger strike has triggered a plea in the Delhi High Court seeking 'force-feeding' of the activist, with petitioners warning he may die within two days. The government has been criticised for ignoring the fast, with CJP's Abhijeet Dipke calling it 'cruel'. The strike has also drawn political attention, though the Congress party is reportedly wary of aligning with Wangchuk's movement, referred to in reports as the 'Cockroach Janta Party'. Wangchuk has been demanding greater autonomy and statehood for Ladakh.
stories.lens: Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike over Ladakh's statehood demand has now escalated to a potential medical and legal crisis, putting pressure on the central government to respond before his condition becomes irreversible.
stories.article:
Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike over Ladakh's political future has reached a critical juncture, with a petition filed in the Delhi High Court warning that the activist may die within two days and seeking judicial intervention in the form of 'force-feeding'. The plea has brought urgent legal scrutiny to a fast that the government has so far appeared to ignore.

CJP's Abhijeet Dipke publicly condemned the government's silence, calling it 'cruel' to ignore a citizen's hunger strike that has attracted national attention. The petition's language — that Wangchuk 'may die in 2 days' — underscores the severity of his physical condition and the urgency felt by supporters and legal advocates.

Wangchuk, a prominent Ladakhi innovator and activist known internationally for his climate work, has been demanding constitutional safeguards for Ladakh, including statehood and inclusion in the Sixth Schedule, which would provide tribal land protections. His cause has resonated widely among residents of the Union Territory, who have felt disenfranchised since Ladakh's bifurcation from Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

Politically, the situation has placed opposition parties in a delicate position. Reports indicate that the Congress party is wary of openly supporting Wangchuk's movement. As legal pressure mounts and the activist's health hangs in the balance, all eyes are on whether the Centre will open dialogue before the courts are forced to intervene.

stories.headline: Air India Crash Investigation Report Likely Ready by October, Say Investigators
stories.what: Investigators probing the Air India crash have indicated that the final report into the accident is likely to be ready by October, according to BBC reporting. The timeline gives a clearer picture of when India and the aviation world can expect authoritative findings on what caused the disaster. The crash, one of the most significant aviation tragedies involving an Indian carrier in recent years, prompted widespread calls for a thorough and transparent inquiry. The October deadline will be closely watched by victims' families, aviation regulators and the airline industry.
stories.lens: The October timeline for the Air India crash report matters to hundreds of grieving families seeking answers — and to India's aviation regulator, which needs the findings to determine systemic safety reforms.
stories.article:
Investigators probing the Air India crash have said the final accident report is likely to be ready by October, offering the clearest official timeline yet for the conclusion of one of Indian aviation's most closely watched inquiries. The BBC reported the development, citing investigators familiar with the probe's progress.

The crash, which sent shockwaves through India's aviation sector, triggered a sweeping investigation involving Indian authorities and international aviation bodies. The complexity of such probes — involving flight data recorder analysis, cockpit voice recordings, structural examination and witness accounts — typically means final reports take many months to complete.

For the families of those who lost their lives, the October target represents a significant milestone: a formal, authoritative account of what went wrong and, crucially, what systemic factors may have contributed to the tragedy. Victims' relatives have consistently demanded transparency and accountability from both the airline and the regulator.

For India's civil aviation authority and Air India itself — undergoing a major transformation under Tata Group ownership — the findings will have direct regulatory and reputational implications. The report is expected to include safety recommendations that could reshape maintenance protocols, crew training requirements, and operational procedures across Indian carriers.

Investigators confirmed the timeline to BBC
Report will include safety recommendations for Indian aviation

stories.headline: Gurugram Woman Runs Over Domestic Worker, Returns Body to Accident Spot After Hospital Declares Her Dead
stories.what: In a deeply disturbing incident from Gurugram, a woman ran over her domestic worker with her vehicle and, after the hospital declared the worker dead, returned the body to the accident spot. The shocking act raises serious questions about the driver's attempt to evade responsibility for the fatal accident. The domestic worker's death and the subsequent conduct of the employer have triggered outrage and a police investigation. The case has reignited concerns about the precarious situation of domestic workers in India, who often have little legal protection.
stories.lens: This Gurugram case exposes the vulnerability of India's millions of unregistered domestic workers — who have minimal legal protections — and the brazen lengths to which employers can go to escape accountability for their deaths.
stories.article:
A woman in Gurugram ran over her domestic worker with her vehicle and, after taking the injured worker to a hospital where she was declared dead, returned the body to the accident spot — an act that police are now investigating as a potential attempt to evade culpability. The case has triggered widespread outrage.

The sequence of events, as reported by The New Indian Express, paints a picture of calculated conduct following a fatal accident. Rather than cooperating with authorities or remaining at the hospital, the employer allegedly transported the deceased back to the site of the collision — a move that investigators believe may have been intended to distance herself from the death.

The case has drawn sharp attention to the plight of domestic workers in India, a largely informal workforce of millions who typically operate without written contracts, formal employment protections, or access to compensation in the event of injury or death. The power imbalance between employers and domestic employees remains a persistent concern for labour rights advocates.

Gurugram police have registered a case and are investigating the full circumstances of the accident and the employer's subsequent conduct. Activists and legal experts are calling for stringent action under applicable laws, and are demanding that the case be treated with the seriousness it deserves given the evidence of deliberate conduct after a preventable death.

Domestic worker was declared dead at hospital
Employer allegedly returned the body to the accident spot
Police investigation underway

stories.headline: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Its First AI Model
stories.what: Thinking Machines Lab, a new artificial intelligence research outfit, has publicly released its first model, marking its formal entry into the competitive AI landscape. The launch signals the continued proliferation of AI labs and model developers beyond the established players such as OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Details on the model's specific capabilities and benchmarks were not disclosed in the available reporting, but the release represents a notable new voice in the field.
stories.lens: The steady emergence of new AI labs releasing capable models means that AI tools are becoming more diverse and accessible — expanding options for Indian developers and startups who may not want to depend solely on a handful of US giants.
stories.article:
Thinking Machines Lab has launched its first artificial intelligence model, entering a field already crowded with heavyweights and fast-moving challengers. The release marks the lab's debut as a public model provider, adding to the diverse ecosystem of AI developers now competing for developer and enterprise attention.

The proliferation of new AI labs has been one of the defining dynamics of the past year. Backed by a combination of venture capital and talent departing from established organisations, dozens of new outfits have launched with ambitions to build frontier-level models. Thinking Machines Lab's first release positions it as one to watch, even if its full capabilities and benchmarks remain to be assessed by the wider research community.

For the AI industry, each new entrant matters not just commercially but scientifically. Competition drives experimentation with different architectures, training approaches, and deployment philosophies — and breakthroughs have come from unexpected quarters, as DeepSeek demonstrated earlier this year.

For Indian developers, enterprises, and AI researchers, a widening field of capable model providers is broadly positive. It increases competitive pressure on pricing, encourages open-source releases, and reduces dependence on any single foreign platform — all factors that matter as India builds out its own AI-driven digital infrastructure.
key_facts: Thinking Machines Lab has released its first AI model
The lab is a new entrant in the competitive AI development space
Joins a wave of new AI labs challenging established players

stories.headline: Apple Gets Green Light for iPhone AI in China — With Alibaba and Baidu on Board
stories.what: Apple has received regulatory approval to roll out its iPhone AI features in China, partnering with domestic tech giants Alibaba and Baidu to comply with the country's strict AI governance rules. The approval marks a significant breakthrough for Apple in its largest overseas market, where foreign AI services face heavy restrictions. China requires AI products to pass government reviews before public deployment, making local partnerships essential for any foreign company seeking to offer AI-driven features.
stories.lens: For Indian tech watchers and Apple users, this signals how AI features on iPhones will vary sharply by geography — and how China's regulatory model could influence other governments, including India's, in demanding local partners for foreign AI.
stories.article:
Apple has secured Chinese government approval to deploy its iPhone AI capabilities in the country, with Alibaba and Baidu serving as the local partners powering the features. The approval clears a major regulatory hurdle that had delayed the rollout of Apple's AI offerings in one of its most critical markets.

China requires all AI services to undergo a rigorous government review process before reaching consumers. Foreign companies, in particular, cannot simply port over their existing AI infrastructure — they must work through approved domestic partners. For Apple, that has meant collaborating with two of China's biggest technology companies: e-commerce and cloud giant Alibaba, and search and AI leader Baidu.

The move is commercially significant for Apple, which has faced intense competition in China from homegrown smartphone brands such as Huawei. Bringing AI features to Chinese iPhones could help Apple reclaim ground with premium consumers who have been drawn to locally developed AI experiences on rival devices.

The development also underscores a broader global trend: AI is becoming a geopolitical and regulatory battlefield as much as a technology race. Governments are increasingly demanding that AI products either be built locally or deeply integrated with domestic players before they can reach citizens — a dynamic that tech companies around the world, including those eyeing India's growing market, will need to navigate carefully.
key_facts: Apple approved to launch iPhone AI features in China
Partners: Alibaba and Baidu to provide local AI infrastructure
China requires government review for all AI products before deployment
Approval helps Apple compete against Huawei and local Android rivals

stories.headline: Apple Stock Jumps Over 3% on Report of iPhone Maker Eyeing AI Chip Acquisitions
stories.what: Apple's stock surged over 3% after reports emerged that the company is exploring acquisitions in the AI chip space. The move signals Apple's intent to deepen its hardware capabilities for artificial intelligence, building on its existing in-house silicon strengths. The report comes on the same day that Apple received approval to launch iPhone AI features in China, making it a significant day of AI-related news for the tech giant.
stories.lens: Apple's chip ambitions directly affect the global AI hardware race — and for Indian consumers and investors tracking technology stocks, a stronger Apple AI ecosystem typically translates into more powerful, capable iPhones reaching Indian shores.
stories.article:
Apple shares jumped over 3% after a report surfaced that the iPhone maker is actively exploring acquisitions in the AI chip sector. The stock movement reflects investor confidence that Apple is preparing to significantly accelerate its artificial intelligence hardware strategy beyond its existing in-house chip development.

Apple has long designed its own silicon — including the A-series chips in iPhones and M-series chips in Macs — giving it a competitive edge in on-device processing. A targeted AI chip acquisition would suggest Apple is looking to fast-track specific capabilities, potentially in areas like neural processing or inference hardware, rather than developing everything from scratch.

The news arrives at a moment when the AI chip market is fiercely contested. Nvidia has dominated AI training infrastructure, while rivals including AMD, Intel, and a wave of startups are vying for a share of both cloud and edge AI compute. An Apple move into acquisitions in this space would mark a notable escalation.

For Indian consumers, Apple's AI hardware push is significant: the company's ability to run sophisticated AI tasks directly on the device — without sending data to the cloud — has been a key differentiator it is trying to extend. A stronger AI chip foundation would make future iPhones meaningfully more capable, potentially widening the gap with Android rivals in on-device intelligence.

Report says Apple is eyeing AI chip acquisitions
Apple already designs in-house A-series and M-series chips
AI chip market dominated by Nvidia, with growing competition

stories.headline: DeepSeek Founder Liang Wenfeng Surpasses Dario Amodei and Greg Brockman as World's Richest AI Founder
stories.what: Liang Wenfeng, the founder of Chinese AI company DeepSeek, has overtaken Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman to become the world's wealthiest AI founder. The rise is striking given that both Amodei and Brockman's respective employers had previously complained to the US government about DeepSeek's competitive threat. DeepSeek made global headlines earlier this year when its low-cost AI model rattled Silicon Valley and challenged assumptions about the resources needed to build frontier AI.
stories.lens: DeepSeek's rise — built on leaner, cost-efficient AI — directly challenges the trillion-dollar spending narrative of US tech giants and has implications for how India and the world think about accessible, affordable AI development.
stories.article:
Liang Wenfeng, founder of Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, has emerged as the world's richest AI founder, surpassing Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Greg Brockman in wealth rankings. The milestone is a remarkable turn for a figure whose company both Amodei and Brockman had flagged to the United States government as a competitive and national-security concern.

DeepSeek burst into global consciousness when it released an AI model that performed at levels comparable to leading American systems but at a fraction of the cost. The release triggered a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks and forced a rethink across the industry about whether massive compute spending was truly a prerequisite for cutting-edge AI.

The irony of DeepSeek's founder now outranking the very American executives who sought Washington's intervention against his company is hard to miss. It reflects both the rapid appreciation in value assigned to Chinese AI ventures and the growing recognition that the AI race is genuinely global — not confined to a handful of well-funded US laboratories.

For observers in India and across the developing world, DeepSeek's trajectory offers an alternative model: that efficient, resourceful engineering can compete with brute-force capital. Whether Liang Wenfeng's ascent translates into lasting geopolitical influence in AI will depend on how the US-China technology standoff evolves in the months ahead.
key_facts: Liang Wenfeng is now the world's richest AI founder
He surpassed Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Greg Brockman
Amodei and Brockman had complained about DeepSeek to the US government
DeepSeek's low-cost AI model previously rattled global markets

stories.headline: Google Sued Over Using Copyrighted Books to Train Gemini AI
stories.what: Google is facing a lawsuit alleging that it used copyrighted books without authorisation to train its Gemini AI model. The case adds to a growing wave of intellectual property litigation targeting major AI companies over the use of human-created content in building large language models. Authors and publishers have increasingly turned to the courts to challenge the AI industry's widespread practice of scraping vast text datasets, and a ruling against Google could reshape how AI models are built and licensed globally.
stories.lens: As Indian publishers, authors, and software companies begin contributing to AI training datasets — often without consent or compensation — this lawsuit sets a legal precedent that could define the rights of creators everywhere, including in India.
stories.article:
Google has been sued over allegations that it used copyrighted books without permission to train its Gemini artificial intelligence model, in the latest intellectual property case targeting a major technology company's AI development practices.

The lawsuit joins a rapidly expanding body of litigation in which authors, news organisations, and other content creators are challenging AI companies for harvesting their work as training data without seeking licences or paying compensation. Cases have been filed against OpenAI, Meta, and others, but a case targeting Gemini — Google's flagship AI product — carries particular weight given the company's scale and the model's widespread deployment.

At the heart of these cases is a fundamental question about copyright in the age of AI: does feeding a book, article, or piece of code into a machine-learning system constitute a reproduction or derivative use that requires the rightsholder's permission? The AI industry has generally argued that training on publicly available data constitutes fair use; rights holders strongly disagree.

For the broader AI ecosystem, the outcome of cases like this one could be transformative. If courts rule that training data must be licensed, the cost and complexity of building large language models would rise dramatically — potentially consolidating power among the largest players who can afford compliance. Indian courts and policymakers are watching these international proceedings closely as they shape India's own emerging AI regulatory framework.
key_facts: Google sued for allegedly using copyrighted books to train Gemini AI
Case is part of a broader wave of IP litigation against AI companies
Central legal question: does AI training on copyrighted content require a licence?
Similar suits filed against OpenAI and Meta

stories.headline: ICC mulls double India-Pakistan World Cup clash as new tournament format takes shape
stories.what: The ICC is considering a dramatic shake-up to the Cricket World Cup format that could see India and Pakistan face each other not once but potentially twice — or even three times — in the same tournament. Reports from The Guardian and Times of India outline a proposed restructuring that would place the two rivals in the same group and also set up a potential knockout rematch. The move would be one of the most significant changes to the tournament's structure in recent memory.
stories.lens: For Indian cricket fans, an India-Pakistan World Cup double-header would be the biggest sporting spectacle in years — and a commercial goldmine for broadcasters and the ICC alike.
stories.article:
The ICC is exploring a fundamental restructuring of the Cricket World Cup format that could deliver Indian and Pakistani fans the prospect of their teams meeting twice — or possibly three times — in a single tournament, according to reports by The Guardian and Times of India.

Under the proposed format, India and Pakistan would be placed in the same group stage, guaranteeing at least one meeting in the league phase. The structure would then be designed so that a knockout-stage rematch becomes a realistic possibility, with some interpretations suggesting a third encounter could theoretically follow if both sides advance deep into the competition. The exact mechanics of the revised format are still being worked through by ICC officials.

The shake-up would represent one of the most consequential changes to World Cup architecture in years. India versus Pakistan matches are consistently the most-watched cricket fixtures on the planet, routinely drawing television audiences in the hundreds of millions and commanding extraordinary broadcast and sponsorship premiums. Any format that multiplies those encounters carries enormous commercial appeal for the global governing body.

Adding a geopolitical dimension, Sri Lanka's sports minister confirmed separately that the island nation remains willing to host India-Pakistan sporting events, signalling that neutral venues are available should bilateral political tensions require it.

For fans, the prospect of a guaranteed India-Pakistan group clash followed by a potential knockout rematch transforms the World Cup into an event of almost unimaginable magnitude. The ICC is expected to finalise format details ahead of the next major cycle, and selectors, broadcasters and boards alike will be watching closely.
key_facts: India and Pakistan could meet twice or three times in one World Cup
Proposed format places both teams in the same group stage
ICC yet to officially confirm the new structure
Sri Lanka signals willingness to host India-Pakistan matches

stories.headline: The day Harrogate 'burst at the seams' when India and Pakistan came to town
stories.what: The Guardian's cricket column The Spin revisits a remarkable historical moment when Harrogate, a small English town, found itself hosting India and Pakistan — an occasion so overwhelmingly attended that the venue reportedly 'burst at the seams'. The piece evokes the deep emotional and cultural charge that any India-Pakistan cricket encounter carries, particularly among the diaspora in England, and places the rivalry in a broader historical and social context.
stories.lens: As the ICC considers multiplying India-Pakistan World Cup encounters, this piece is a vivid reminder of just how culturally electrifying — and logistically challenging — those fixtures have always been.
stories.article:
The Guardian's celebrated cricket column The Spin has turned the clock back to a memorable chapter in cricket history: the day the English town of Harrogate could barely contain itself when India and Pakistan arrived to play, with the venue reportedly 'bursting at the seams' under the weight of a passionate, largely diaspora crowd.

The piece speaks to something deeper than sport. India-Pakistan encounters have always carried the weight of partition, migration, identity and longing — nowhere more viscerally than among South Asian communities settled in Britain, for whom these matches are among the most emotionally loaded sporting events imaginable. The image of a genteel Yorkshire spa town overwhelmed by the fervour of the subcontinent is both comic and deeply moving.

The timing of the column is pointed. With the ICC now reportedly exploring a World Cup format that could deliver India-Pakistan clashes multiple times in one tournament, The Spin's nostalgic revisit serves as a reminder that this rivalry is not simply a commercial product — it is a living, breathing cultural phenomenon that has been drawing extraordinary crowds and emotions for decades.

For everyday Indian readers, the story is a bridge between the past and the present: the same passions that once packed out a small Yorkshire ground are the forces that today make an India-Pakistan World Cup double the most-anticipated fixture in global sport.

The Guardian's The Spin column revisits the historic occasion
Story contextualises the India-Pakistan rivalry's deep cultural roots
Column published amid ICC discussions on multiplying World Cup encounters

Ben Stokes has returned to Durham County Cricket Club with what the club has described as a 'new lease of life', marking a significant personal chapter for one of the most influential cricketers of his generation following his retirement from England's one-day international setup.

Stokes stepped away from ODI cricket to manage his workload and mental well-being, a decision that drew widespread respect within the game. His return to Durham suggests the 32-year-old is finding renewed purpose at the county level, away from the pressures of an unrelenting international calendar that had stretched him to his limits.

While Stokes remains England's Test captain and a cornerstone of their red-ball ambitions, his absence from the ODI arena has reshaped England's 50-over team. Ben Duckett and a younger generation of English batters are now being asked to carry the white-ball side, as Duckett himself acknowledged ahead of the ongoing second ODI against India.

Stokes's story resonates far beyond English cricket. The debate over player workload and mental health is equally pressing in India, where the BCCI juggles an enormous schedule across all three formats for its top stars. His willingness to step back, recharge, and return on his own terms has set a precedent that players and boards worldwide are watching carefully.

The first look of Haiwaan landed on Tuesday evening, and it immediately set the tone for what could be one of Bollywood's most charged thrillers in recent memory. Akshay Kumar is seen wearing a smile that radiates cold menace, while Saif Ali Khan delivers a portrait of brooding intensity — his eyes carrying the full weight of a character that clearly operates in the shadows.

The contrast between the two stars is the visual centrepiece of the reveal. Where Akshay projects an unsettling cheerfulness, Saif's stillness suggests something far more dangerous lurking beneath the surface. Together, the first look frames the film as a clash of two formidable forces, each projecting a distinct brand of threat.

The title — meaning 'beast' in Urdu — only adds to the primal energy the film appears to be going for.

Details about the plot, director, and release date remain closely guarded for now. But if the first look is any indication, the makers are betting on the chemistry of opposites — and on the proven box-office pull of two stars who know exactly how to own a frame.

stories.headline: Anurag Kashyap Says Censor Chief Prasoon Joshi Has Not Seen Satluj, Yet Blocked It
stories.what: Director Anurag Kashyap has publicly accused Central Board of Film Certification chief Prasoon Joshi of not having watched Satluj before raising objections that led to the film's ban. Kashyap's blunt charge — 'Prasoon Joshi has not seen Satluj, but has problems with it' — strikes at the heart of how India's film certification process functions, raising questions about due process in censorship decisions. The controversy has reignited a longstanding debate about creative freedom and institutional accountability in Bollywood.
stories.lens: When a filmmaker accuses the country's top censor of banning a film he hasn't watched, it raises urgent questions about how creative work gets blocked in India — something every filmmaker and film-goer should care about.
stories.article:
Anurag Kashyap has launched a pointed attack on Prasoon Joshi, the chairman of the Central Board of Film Certification, claiming that Joshi had not even watched the film Satluj before objecting to it and effectively causing its ban. 'Prasoon Joshi has not seen Satluj, but has problems with it,' Kashyap said, in remarks that swiftly drew attention across the film industry.

The allegation, if accurate, would amount to a serious procedural failure at India's apex film certification body. Kashyap, one of Hindi cinema's most vocal advocates for creative freedom, has long been a critic of what he views as arbitrary and politically motivated censorship. His latest salvo suggests that the ban on Satluj was handed down without the board's chairman engaging directly with the film's content.

The CBFC has not publicly responded to Kashyap's charge. Prasoon Joshi, a lyricist and advertising veteran appointed to head the board, has in the past emphasised a balanced approach to certification. But Kashyap's accusation cuts through that framing, implying that decision-making at the top level of the board can be detached from the actual viewing experience.

The row over Satluj adds to a growing list of films that have faced certification hurdles in recent years, prompting recurring calls from filmmakers for a more transparent, rules-bound process. For Kashyap, however, the fight is far from over — his parting words underlined the defiance: 'Ladai aage tak ladni hai.'
key_facts: Kashyap alleges Prasoon Joshi did not watch Satluj before blocking it
Film Satluj has been banned by the CBFC
Prasoon Joshi is chairman of the Central Board of Film Certification

stories.headline: Shabana Azmi Urges Sonam Wangchuk to End Hunger Strike: 'Ladai Aage Tak Ladni Hai'
stories.what: Veteran actress and activist Shabana Azmi has publicly appealed to climate activist and Ladakh champion Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike, saying 'Ladai aage tak ladni hai' — the fight must go on. Azmi's intervention highlights the growing solidarity from Bollywood and the arts community with Wangchuk's ongoing campaign for Ladakh's rights and statehood. The appeal underscores how the protest has moved beyond regional politics to command national cultural attention.
stories.lens: When prominent voices from India's cultural world appeal to a hunger striker, it both amplifies the cause and reflects how deeply Ladakh's political status has resonated beyond the region.
stories.article:
Veteran actress and prominent public voice Shabana Azmi stepped into the debate around Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike on Tuesday, urging the Ladakhi activist to preserve his health and live to fight another day. 'Ladai aage tak ladni hai,' Azmi said — the fight must be taken forward — in a message that combined solidarity with concern.

Wangchuk, the engineer, educator, and climate activist who became globally known as an inspiration for the film 3 Idiots, has been on a hunger strike demanding statehood and constitutional protections for Ladakh. His protest has drawn attention to the region's unique vulnerabilities following its bifurcation from Jammu & Kashmir in 2019 and its designation as a Union Territory without a legislature.

Azmi's appeal adds to a chorus of voices from India's arts and entertainment world expressing support for Wangchuk's cause. Earlier in the day, filmmaker Anurag Kashyap also publicly stood with Wangchuk, questioning the government's continued silence on the activist's demands. Together, these interventions signal a broadening of the movement's cultural footprint.

For Wangchuk's supporters, Azmi's words carry the weight of a long career spent speaking out on social and political issues. Whether her appeal — and those of others in the cultural sphere — will translate into government engagement with his demands remains to be seen.
key_facts: Shabana Azmi publicly urges Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike
Wangchuk is protesting for Ladakh's statehood and constitutional protections
Anurag Kashyap also voiced support for Wangchuk the same day
